newsitem.title: CHINA: China to issue new futures regulations this year.
newsitem.headline: China to issue new futures regulations this year.

text.p: China plans to issue five sets of regulations governing its futures market in the first half of this year to standardise its chaotic markets, the Overseas Edition of the People's Daily said on Monday.

Three new rules being drafted by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), China's top watchdog, would include temporary regulations on futures trading and management of futures brokers, the newspaper said.
Two other sets of regulations being jointly drafted by the commission and the Finance Ministry would cover accounting and financial matters related to futures trading, it said.

"The new regulations will make up for management weaknesses before the issue of a futures markets law," the newspaper said without elaborating. China's futures law has been delayed over disagreement of what it should cover.
The CSRC would also explore ways to merge some of China's 14 futures exchanges or link them electronically, the newspaper said.
Industry officials have said there are too many exchanges and their number eventually might be reduced to four or five.
The securities commission would also carry out nationwide annual checks to prevent uncontrolled competition among brokers, the newspaper said but gave no further details.
